title: ICE Detains More Than 100 in Overnight Raid at Memphis Bar, Advocates Call It City's Largest
detail: ICE and Homeland Security Investigations, joined by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, conducted a multi-agency operation around 1 a.m. on August 30, 2026 at El Corralón, a Latin American bar and restaurant at 3870 Macon Road in Memphis's Berclair neighborhood, arriving with a fleet of rented buses. ICE said the operation stemmed from an investigation into alleged illegal gambling machines and drug activity at the establishment, but immigrant advocacy group Vecindarios901 said over 100 people were detained and described it as the largest immigration raid in Memphis history. The Memphis Police Department said it was not involved in planning or carrying out the operation, providing only traffic and crowd-control support after the fact; the Memphis Safe Task Force was not involved. Witnesses reported ICE agents intimidating bystanders into deleting recordings and shining lights into cameras to discourage filming, and described children left waiting for parents who did not return home. Mayor Paul Young called the operation 'unsettling' and said those detained 'are part of our Memphis community' who 'deserve to be treated with dignity.' Protests followed Sunday evening, and more than 50 local businesses pledged to refuse service to Memphis Safe Task Force members. DHS confirmed on September 1, 2026 that the raid — which it named 'Operation Corral Light' and credited to ICE New Orleans — arrested 121 people with criminal histories including larceny, drug possession, domestic violence, DUI, assault, child endangerment, and prostitution; ICE ERO New Orleans Acting Field Office Director Scott Ladwig said the operation aimed to 'arrest illegal aliens and eliminate drug activity.' A September 5, 2026 NPR follow-up report, citing Vecindarios901, said parents of at least 16 children were among those taken into custody, and that more than a week after the raid DHS had publicly named only 5 of the 121 people arrested while remaining silent on the identities and case details of the other 116.
